title: reorganize-tf-modules-per-environment-and-add-tfstate-migrator
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Private deployments historically used a single monolithic Terraform layout that bundled GPU pools, IAM roles, and networking together with a shared remote state. This made per-environment upgrades risky (apply touches many unrelated resources) and increased the blast radius during rollbacks. This PR restructures TF modules to have clearer separation by workload and environment, introduces a lightweight tfstate migrator script to transition existing customers to per-environment state without downtime, and documents upgrade/rollback procedures. Key goals: 1) split GPU nodepool module from cluster/networking to allow independent lifecycle; 2) extract IAM role policy templates into a reusable module consumed by both private and dedicated workflows; 3) introduce per-environment state layout (env/<env>/<cluster>) and helper scripts to perform safe state moves; 4) add migration safety checks and automated plan verification to CI; 5) keep change surface minimal for customers that opt out of migration. This description includes the high-level design, migration steps, risk model, and QA results. Migration steps: 1) run scripts/tfstate-migrator.sh --dry-run against legacy backend to enumerate resources and suggested mapping; 2) create new backend configs under env/<env>/<cluster>/backend.tf; 3) run migrator with --apply to move state to the new backends; 4) run terraform plan against each new backend; 5) roll forward module usage (update root module to reference modules/gpu, modules/iam, modules/network). Rollback: the migrator keeps a stable backup of the source backend and will not delete state from the origin; if verification fails, run migrator --rollback to copy state back. Backwards compatibility: the top-level root module accepts an opt-in variable tfstate_migration = true; default false so existing customers see no change unless they run the migration. Included docs: private-deployments/upgrade-guides/tfstate-split.md with step-by-step commands and smoke-test checklists. Testing & QA: ran migration dry-run on a large internal staging cluster (approx 120 GPU nodes) and validated zero-downtime restarts and identical resource digests; CI now includes an extra job that performs a plan against a mocked per-env backend after changes. Security: IAM module templates were parameterized to avoid granting overly broad permissions; added unit tests for policy json generation. Related: ENG-9251 (state-migrations), PM-417 (private-deploy rollout).

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Overall looks good, main concern is ensuring no implicit provider alias changes. Please document provider alias expectations and add a test that validates provider alias remains constant during the migrator run.
Asha Patel: Added provider alias note to docs and expanded migrator dry-run output to include provider aliases. Also added a small unit test to mock provider metadata.
Elliot Chen: Verified migration on staging cluster; minor nit in IAM policy tests (tighten S3 resource ARNs) — pushed fix in a9e3f40.
Samira Khan: Approved after CI green and manual smoke tests passed. Left a suggestion to add telemetry events for migration start/finish — filing follow-up ENG-9405.
release_notes: Split Terraform state per environment and introduced a safe tfstate migrator. Customers can opt into per-env state to reduce blast radius for upgrades. IAM policies refactored into reusable module. Includes upgrade guidance and rollback procedure. (Non-breaking by default)
risk_assessment: Low-medium: default behavior unchanged; migration is opt-in. The migrator does remote state copies and preserves backups. Recommended that customers test in staging before applying to prod.
testing_summary: Ran full dry-run migration on internal staging (120 GPUs). Verified terraform plan equivalence post-migration and ran smoke tests for pod scheduling and KV cache reconnects. CI job tf-plan-per-env added to prevent regressions.
notes_for_ops: Ops should coordinate with customers to schedule migration windows. The migrator requires access to both source and destination backends and will write a backup file to the origin bucket. Keep at least 14 days retention on origin backend until migration is validated.
hotfix_followup: None required. If migration fails, run scripts/tfstate-migrator.sh --rollback which re-copies state to the source backend and verifies integrity.
